title: Project design configuration format and inspection boundary
question: Which configuration boundary should declare Meridian project inspection inputs and Design System adapters?

scope.summary: Choose a versioned, inspectable project configuration format without hiding UI Generation ownership inside package metadata or heuristic inference.
outOfScope: Final external Design System adapter selection

constraints: Explicit configuration must remain distinguishable from inferred findings.
The loader must not require a new runtime dependency for the initial Node implementation.
Project-existing Design System adapters must remain higher priority than external defaults.

criteria.name: Schema validation
criteria.description: Supports a versioned strict contract and deterministic machine validation.

criteria.name: Runtime and dependency cost
criteria.description: Can be loaded by the current Node tooling without adding a parser dependency or executable configuration.

criteria.name: Responsibility separation
criteria.description: Keeps UI Generation configuration separate from package publication and runtime module semantics.

criteria.name: Discoverability
criteria.description: Has one predictable project-root location and can link directly to its schema.

criteria.name: Interoperability
criteria.description: Aligns with JSON-based repository metadata and DTCG token interchange without custom coercion.

criteria.name: Human editing
criteria.description: Can be reviewed and edited without generated code or hidden defaults.

candidates.name: Dedicated meridian.design.json sidecar
candidates.license: Format specifications are public; Meridian schema and loader remain repository-owned.

assessments.notes: The checked-in strict Draft 2020-12 schema validates the complete configuration.
Node parses JSON without an added dependency and the local validator already supports the used keywords.
The sidecar does not alter package runtime or publication metadata.
One project-root filename and a $schema reference provide a deterministic entry point.
Both configuration and the chosen token interchange boundary are JSON-based.
The file is explicit and reviewable, with more punctuation than YAML but no implicit scalar coercion.

limitations: Long adapter declarations are more verbose than YAML.

candidates.name: Custom meridian field in package.json
candidates.license: Uses standard package metadata containers; Meridian would own the custom field contract.

assessments.notes: The custom field can be validated, but whole-file ownership and third-party package schema composition are less direct.
Node parses package.json without another dependency.
UI design inspection becomes coupled to package identity, dependency, publication, and module metadata.
package.json is discoverable but monorepos can contain several competing package boundaries.
JSON is interoperable, but the custom field is irrelevant or noisy to non-Node projects.
The field is editable but competes with unrelated package configuration.

limitations: Couples UI Generation to Node package structure.
Ambiguous ownership in monorepos and non-package project roots.

candidates.name: Dedicated meridian.design.yaml sidecar
candidates.license: YAML specification permits copying; an implementation parser would introduce its own license and update surface.

assessments.notes: A parsed YAML value can be validated, but syntax parsing and schema validation are separate failure surfaces.
The current Node runtime has no built-in YAML parser, so Meridian would add and govern a parser dependency.
A dedicated sidecar keeps project design configuration separate from package metadata.
A fixed project-root sidecar is deterministic.
YAML is cross-language, but DTCG sources and Meridian contracts still cross a JSON conversion boundary.
YAML is concise and supports comments, while indentation and scalar rules require parser-aware editing.

limitations: Requires a parser dependency and security/update review.
Introduces another serialization format beside existing Meridian JSON contracts.

evidence.title: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
evidence.summary: Draft 2020-12 defines the schema dialect and validation vocabulary used by Meridian's strict machine contracts.
limitations: JSON Schema does not choose the surrounding project configuration location.

evidence.title: Node.js Modules: Packages
evidence.summary: Node documents package.json as the boundary for package identity, module type, imports, exports, and package entry points.
limitations: Node documentation does not prohibit unrelated custom fields.

evidence.title: package.json
evidence.summary: npm defines package.json as package metadata covering identity, versions, dependencies, entry points, publication, and platform constraints.
limitations: npm permits additional fields and does not define Meridian ownership.

evidence.title: YAML 1.2.2 Specification
evidence.summary: YAML 1.2.2 defines a human-oriented, cross-language serialization format with indentation-based structure and standard schemas.
limitations: The specification does not provide a parser in the Node standard library.

evidence.title: Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10
evidence.summary: The stable token interchange report uses JSON and recommends .tokens or .tokens.json files for typed design token exchange.
limitations: The token format does not prescribe a complete project inspection configuration.

spikes.title: Project configuration and inspector comparative spike
spikes.hypothesis: A dedicated JSON sidecar can provide strict validation, deterministic loading, evidence-backed inspection, and project-first adapter resolution without a new parser dependency.
findings: The JSON sidecar validates with the existing local Draft 2020-12 subset and loads through the Node standard library.
The generated Project Context is byte-deterministic and binds the configuration digest.
package.json remains evidence for package and module facts instead of becoming the UI Generation configuration owner.
YAML would require a new parser dependency before any project inspection can run.
The spike selects an available project adapter even when an external candidate has a numerically higher priority.

decision.rationale: The dedicated JSON sidecar is the only candidate that combines strict existing-schema validation, zero new runtime dependencies, a predictable root entry point, and separation from package publication metadata.
tradeoffs: JSON is more verbose than YAML and does not support comments.
Projects must add one Meridian-specific root file.
A future non-JSON authoring layer must still compile to this validated contract.
unresolvedItems: Human approval is required before the 0.1.0 config filename and shape become a stable public contract.
revisitTriggers: Node gains a standard safe YAML parser
A cross-tool project design configuration standard emerges
Non-Node projects cannot adopt the JSON sidecar without material duplication
The config grows beyond a reviewable project-level boundary
